es: Reconocer cómo se estructura una historia para inspirar, advertir o convencer, señalar el momento que revela su propósito e inferir la postura del narrador.

vocabulary.es: relato con moraleja, historia de advertencia
dejar clara la idea, remachar el mensaje

teaching.en: A compelling story has an arc: a situation, a problem, a turning point and an outcome, and the audience waits for the last part with growing curiosity.
teaching.es: Una historia cautivadora tiene un arco: una situación, un problema, un giro y un desenlace, y la audiencia espera la última parte con curiosidad creciente.
teaching.explanationEs: Arc es la forma de la historia; outcome es cómo termina; compelling = difícil de dejar de escuchar.
segments: A compelling story has an arc: a situation, a problem, a turning point and
an outcome, and the audience waits for the last part with growing curiosity.
teaching.audioText: A compelling story has an arc: a situation, a problem, a turning point and an outcome, and the audience waits for the last part with growing curiosity.

teaching.en: A story can inspire: the speaker fails twice, then finds a way, and the audience leaves with more hope than it brought into the room.
teaching.es: Una historia puede inspirar: el narrador fracasa dos veces, luego encuentra un camino y la audiencia sale con más esperanza de la que trajo.
teaching.explanationEs: Inspire busca una emoción positiva; audience es el público que escucha.
segments: A story can inspire: the speaker fails twice, then finds a way, and
the audience leaves with more hope than it brought into the room.
teaching.audioText: A story can inspire: the speaker fails twice, then finds a way, and the audience leaves with more hope than it brought into the room.

teaching.en: A cautionary tale is meant to warn: it shows a mistake and its price, as in 'I ignored the noise, and the car stopped on a dark road.'
teaching.es: Un relato con moraleja está hecho para advertir: muestra un error y su precio, como en «Ignoré el ruido y el coche se paró en una carretera oscura».
teaching.explanationEs: Warn = avisar de un peligro; lo que importa es el error y lo que cuesta.
segments: A cautionary tale is meant to warn: it shows a mistake and its price,
as in 'I ignored the noise, and the car stopped on a dark road.'
teaching.audioText: A cautionary tale is meant to warn: it shows a mistake and its price, as in 'I ignored the noise, and the car stopped on a dark road.'

teaching.en: A story can also persuade, because the listener sees the result instead of hearing an argument: 'Our shop nearly closed, until one change saved it.'
teaching.es: Una historia también puede convencer, porque el oyente ve el resultado en lugar de oír un argumento: «Nuestra tienda casi cierra, hasta que un cambio la salvó».
teaching.explanationEs: Persuade = convencer a alguien de hacer algo.
segments: A story can also persuade, because the listener sees the result instead of
hearing an argument: 'Our shop nearly closed, until one change saved it.'
teaching.audioText: A story can also persuade, because the listener sees the result instead of hearing an argument: 'Our shop nearly closed, until one change saved it.'

teaching.en: After the setback, the lesson appears: 'That winter taught me to ask for help,' and one concrete image helps it resonate long after the talk.
teaching.es: Tras el revés aparece la lección: «Aquel invierno me enseñó a pedir ayuda», y una imagen concreta ayuda a que resuene mucho después de la charla.
teaching.explanationEs: Setback es un contratiempo; lesson casi siempre revela el propósito; resonate = calar.
segments: After the setback, the lesson appears: 'That winter taught me to ask for
help,' and one concrete image helps it resonate long after the talk.
teaching.audioText: After the setback, the lesson appears: 'That winter taught me to ask for help,' and one concrete image helps it resonate long after the talk.

teaching.en: Good speakers do not simply announce the moral: they drive the point home with one final sentence that tells the audience what to do next.
teaching.es: Los buenos oradores no se limitan a anunciar la moraleja: dejan clara la idea con una última frase que dice al público qué hacer a continuación.
teaching.explanationEs: Drive the point home = reforzar el mensaje hasta que no quepa duda.
segments: Good speakers do not simply announce the moral: they drive the point home
with one final sentence that tells the audience what to do next.
teaching.audioText: Good speakers do not simply announce the moral: they drive the point home with one final sentence that tells the audience what to do next.

prompt.es: Decide con qué propósito se cuenta esta historia.

choices.text: To warn the audience about what ignoring problems costs
To inspire the audience with a story of recovery
To persuade the audience to choose a local garage

feedback.es: El narrador muestra un error (ignorar el ruido) y lo que costó; no hay superación heroica ni un servicio que vender, así que la historia advierte.

hint.es: Fíjate en el error y en lo que cuesta.

origin.text: I ignored the noise in the engine for weeks. One night the car stopped on a dark road, forty miles from anywhere, and it took three hours before anyone came. Now I check everything before a long trip.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es decir, seguía el arco clásico de toda historia.»

feedback.es: El arco es la forma de la historia, de la situación inicial al desenlace pasando por el problema y el giro.

hint.es: Es la curva que va de la situación al desenlace.

origin.text: The anecdote began with a calm situation, introduced a problem in the second sentence and ended with a clear outcome. In other words, it followed the classic ___ of a story.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Tras el revés, el equipo aprendió una dura lección.»

answer.text: After the setback the team learned a hard lesson

feedback.es: El revés va primero y la lección llega después: ese orden es el que revela el propósito de la historia.

prompt.es: Escucha la charla y elige con qué propósito y en qué momento se revela.

choices.text: To warn other shops, because her own bakery nearly closed.
To inspire the audience, and her final advice reveals it.
To persuade people to bake, because her orders grew.

feedback.es: Supera el revés del supermercado y termina con un consejo esperanzador; la frase final revela que busca inspirar, no advertir ni vender.

origin.audio: Last month a baker spoke at our community meeting. For years she opened at six, she said, and her bread was the best in the street. Then a supermarket opened next door, and her customers disappeared. She almost gave up. Instead, she began baking for neighbours who could not leave their homes, and within a year she had more orders than ever. She finished by saying, find the people who need you, and they will find you.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada historia breve con su propósito principal.

pairs: A nurse who kept going after failing her exam twice.
A man who lost his savings after ignoring every warning sign.
A school that cut waste by half, with figures for every month.
A list of dates with no problem and no lesson.

feedback.es: Cada historia destaca algo distinto: superar un revés, pagar un error, mostrar un resultado deseable o ningún propósito.

pairs: A nurse who kept going after failing her exam twice.
A man who lost his savings after ignoring every warning sign.
A school that cut waste by half, with figures for every month.
A list of dates with no problem and no lesson.

prompt.es: Elige el momento de la historia que revela su propósito.

choices.text: Then we moved online, and within a year we had customers in six countries.
Our shop was nearly empty, and the winter had been very long.
Today I tell every small business owner I meet: try something new.

feedback.es: La frase final se dirige al público y dice qué debe hacer: ahí se revela que el propósito es persuadir; lo anterior solo cuenta la situación y el desenlace.

origin.text: Our shop was nearly empty, and the winter had been very long. Then we moved online, and within a year we had customers in six countries. Today I tell every small business owner I meet: try something new before you have to.

prompt.es: Lee el final del discurso y elige qué pide realmente la directora a los asistentes.

choices.text: To build links with their neighbours before an emergency arrives.
To give money so that the library and the clinic can be built again.
To learn how to use a boat in case there is a flood.

feedback.es: Ella descarta expresamente la donación y pide conocer a los vecinos: lo que salvó al pueblo no fue el dinero sino las relaciones.

origin.text: When the flood came, we lost the library, the clinic and six years of records. What saved us was not money: it was the neighbours with boats. So I am not asking you for a donation tonight. I am asking you to learn the names of the people on your street.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué la narradora guarda los formularios de los exámenes.

choices.text: They prove that the examiner had been unfair to her.
They remind her that giving up would have been easier.
They show her sister how many times she tried.

feedback.es: Los guarda como recordatorio de que rendirse era lo fácil: es la lección que revela el propósito de inspirar.

origin.audio: I failed my driving test three times. The third time, the examiner looked at me and sighed. I remember thinking that I would never drive. But my sister said, one more try, and I booked it the same afternoon. I passed, hardly believing it. I still keep the failed forms in a drawer, because they remind me that quitting was always the easier choice.

prompt.es: Completa: «La frase final buscaba dejar clara la idea: nadie debe ignorar un aviso.»

feedback.es: Drive the point home es reforzar el mensaje hasta que no haya duda; aquí, con una frase final dirigida al público.

origin.text: The speaker told the story of the night the lights went out on the motorway. Her last sentence was meant to ___ the point home: nobody should ignore a warning light.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Una historia con moraleja muestra un error y el precio que se paga.»

answer.text: A cautionary tale shows a mistake and the price that follows it

feedback.es: Un cautionary tale advierte mostrando el error y su precio, que es la estructura de este relato.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige con qué propósito cuenta la mujer su historia de la empresa.

choices.text: To warn company owners about the risks of selling a business.
To blame the workers for taking such a great risk.
To persuade listeners that the same plan could work for them.

feedback.es: La frase final traslada el resultado al pueblo del oyente: el propósito es convencerle de que puede repetirse, no advertir ni criticar.

origin.audio: Everyone expected our town to lose its biggest company. Instead, the workers bought it. In the first year they lost money and nearly gave up. But they learned to sell directly to customers, and the company now gives jobs to two hundred people. If it worked here, I believe it can work in your town too.

prompt.es: Completa: «La historia resonó con el público porque todos habían vivido un revés así.»

feedback.es: Resonate con el público significa que la historia toca algo que los oyentes reconocen como propio.

origin.text: The outcome was not what they had hoped for, but the story still ___ with the audience because everyone in the room had faced a setback of some kind.

prompt.es: Lee la reseña y elige qué le reprocha el crítico a la oradora.

choices.text: That the story had no clear purpose or final lesson.
That she told the story without any real emotion.
That the audience did not stay until the very end.

feedback.es: El crítico habla de una historia emotiva pero sin conclusión: no hubo lección ni petición, así que el público no supo qué se esperaba de él.

origin.text: The speaker told a moving story about losing her business, yet she offered no conclusion from it. We waited for the lesson; it never came. The audience left politely, without knowing what she wanted from them.

title.es: Subir lo que está en juego

es: Crear tensión en el inicio de una historia contrastando la rutina pasada (used to, would) con una ruptura en pasado simple y dejando claro lo que está en juego con un condicional.

vocabulary.es: estar en juego, pender de un hilo
mal presentimiento, nudo en el estómago

teaching.en: The stakes are what the character could lose, such as a job, a friendship or a home, and they must be named early so that the audience feels what is on the line.
teaching.es: Lo que está en juego es lo que el personaje podría perder, como un trabajo, una amistad o un hogar, y hay que nombrarlo pronto para que el público sienta lo que se arriesga.
teaching.explanationEs: Stakes es plural en este sentido: «the stakes are high»; on the line = en juego.
segments: The stakes are what the character could lose, such as a job, a friendship or a home,
and they must be named early so that the audience feels what is on the line.
teaching.audioText: The stakes are what the character could lose, such as a job, a friendship or a home, and they must be named early so that the audience feels what is on the line.

teaching.en: Back then we used to open at eight, and we would drink tea before the first customer arrived, in the quiet mornings that our routine had always given us.
teaching.es: Entonces solíamos abrir a las ocho y tomábamos té antes de que llegara el primer cliente, en las tranquilas mañanas que nuestra rutina siempre nos había dado.
teaching.explanationEs: Used to y would describen hábitos pasados; would solo con acciones, nunca con estados.
segments: Back then we used to open at eight, and we would drink tea before the
first customer arrived, in the quiet mornings that our routine had always given us.
teaching.audioText: Back then we used to open at eight, and we would drink tea before the first customer arrived, in the quiet mornings that our routine had always given us.

teaching.en: Then a letter arrived, and a threat began to loom over everything we had built, even though nobody said a word about it at dinner.
teaching.es: Entonces llegó una carta y una amenaza empezó a cernirse sobre todo lo que habíamos construido, aunque nadie dijo nada durante la cena.
teaching.explanationEs: Then + pasado simple marca la ruptura; threat es la amenaza; loom, que algo malo se acerca.
segments: Then a letter arrived, and a threat began to loom over everything we
had built, even though nobody said a word about it at dinner.
teaching.audioText: Then a letter arrived, and a threat began to loom over everything we had built, even though nobody said a word about it at dinner.

teaching.en: Without warning the risk became real: if we failed to pay by Friday, we would lose the shop, and the future of twelve families would hang in the balance.
teaching.es: Sin previo aviso el riesgo se volvió real: si no pagábamos el viernes, perderíamos la tienda y el futuro de doce familias estaría en juego.
teaching.explanationEs: If + pasado, would + verbo base, expresa el riesgo visto desde el pasado.
segments: Without warning the risk became real: if we failed to pay by Friday, we would
lose the shop, and the future of twelve families would hang in the balance.
teaching.audioText: Without warning the risk became real: if we failed to pay by Friday, we would lose the shop, and the future of twelve families would hang in the balance.

teaching.en: The call did not just disrupt our routine, it left me with a sinking feeling and a growing dread of the weekend.
teaching.es: La llamada no solo alteró nuestra rutina, me dejó con un mal presentimiento y un temor creciente por el fin de semana.
teaching.explanationEs: Disrupt es alterar algo que funcionaba; dread es un miedo que crece con la espera.
segments: The call did not just disrupt our routine, it left me
with a sinking feeling and a growing dread of the weekend.
teaching.audioText: The call did not just disrupt our routine, it left me with a sinking feeling and a growing dread of the weekend.

teaching.en: For years the routine had felt permanent and was simply taken for granted, which is exactly why the letter hit so hard.
teaching.es: Durante años la rutina había parecido permanente y se daba por hecho, y por eso la carta golpeó tan fuerte.
teaching.explanationEs: Taken for granted: algo que se da por seguro y no se valora hasta que está en peligro.
segments: For years the routine had felt permanent and was simply taken
for granted, which is exactly why the letter hit so hard.
teaching.audioText: For years the routine had felt permanent and was simply taken for granted, which is exactly why the letter hit so hard.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que describe una rutina pasada que ya terminó.

choices.text: We were opening the shop at eight when the phone rang.
We used to open the shop at eight and drink tea first.
We have opened the shop at eight every day since the beginning of spring.

feedback.es: «Used to» expresa un hábito pasado que ya no continúa; el pasado continuo es una acción interrumpida y el presente perfecto sigue vigente.

hint.es: Busca el hábito que ya no existe.

origin.text: The narrator is describing the quiet mornings before the trouble started, when nothing seemed likely to change in the little shop by the station.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cada domingo mi abuelo nos llevaba a pescar al río.»

feedback.es: Para una acción repetida en el pasado sirven would y used to.

hint.es: Hábito de acción: hay dos formas posibles.

origin.text: Every Sunday my grandfather ___ take us fishing on the river, and we never came home before dark. Then the doctor told him he had to rest.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Solíamos compartir un piso pequeño encima de la panadería.»

answer.text: We used to share a tiny flat above the bakery

feedback.es: «Used to» va seguido del verbo base: share.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto y «used to».

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué amenaza rompe la rutina y qué podría perderse.

choices.text: The river is flooding, and the villagers could lose all of their houses.
The mayor has resigned, and the village could lose its school.
The river is dirty, and the fishing families could lose their living.

feedback.es: La rutina (nadar y dormir junto al río) se rompe cuando el agua se vuelve negra, y lo que está en juego es el sustento de las familias que pescan y el lugar donde crecieron.

origin.audio: Every summer we would swim in the river, and we used to sleep outside near the water, even when the nights were cold. Nobody worried, because the river had always been clean. Then, one morning, the water turned black, and the smell hung over the whole village. The mayor said that a company further up the river was responsible. If it did not stop, the families who fished would lose their living, and we would lose the place where we had grown up.

prompt.es: Completa: «Éramos felices en esa casa, pero ahora está vacía.»

feedback.es: Be es un estado, por eso se usa used to y no would.

origin.text: The rooms are cold and empty now. We ___ be so happy in that house, but now the garden is full of weeds and nobody has opened the windows for years.

prompt.es: Elige la reescritura que añade lo que está en juego.

choices.text: My parents used to run a small bakery, and we would open at six. Then a man in a suit came, and if they refused to sign, they would lose the shop.
My parents used to run a small bakery, and we would open at six. Then a man in a suit came, and everybody in the kitchen felt very sad and worried about the future.
My parents ran a small bakery, and one morning a man in a suit came to see them, and he was very tall, friendly and kind to everyone in the shop.

feedback.es: Incluye rutina, ruptura y un riesgo concreto con «if… would»; las otras dos no dicen qué se puede perder.

origin.text: My parents ran a small bakery. One morning, a man in a suit came to see them.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué teme perder realmente la narradora.

choices.text: The fishing boat that her grandfather had kept for years.
Their shared mornings and her grandfather's sense of purpose.
Her place at school and the friends she had made.

feedback.es: Teme perder las mañanas juntos y, sobre todo, lo único que hacía sentirse vivo a su abuelo: lo que está en juego es emocional, no material.

origin.audio: My grandfather would wake me at five, and we used to fish until noon. Then the doctor said that he must not walk the river path again. I was afraid that I would lose our mornings together, and, worse, that he would lose the only thing that made him feel alive. For weeks I pretended that nothing had changed.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué revela «I pretended that nothing had changed».

choices.text: She had forgotten what the doctor had said about the river path.
She was angry with her grandfather for following the doctor's advice.
She was trying to keep the routine alive to protect them both.

feedback.es: Fingir que nada había cambiado es un modo de proteger la rutina y de evitar que el miedo se haga real para los dos.

origin.audio: My grandfather would wake me at five, and we used to fish until noon. Then the doctor said that he must not walk the river path again. I was afraid that I would lose our mornings together, and, worse, that he would lose the only thing that made him feel alive. For weeks I pretended that nothing had changed.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si la carta llegaba tarde, perderíamos la tienda.»

feedback.es: El riesgo se expresa con «if» + pasado simple en la condición y «would» + verbo base en la consecuencia.

origin.text: We had never missed a payment in twenty years. If the letter ___ late, we would lose the shop, and that was the risk we lived with every day of that winter.

prompt.es: Escribe un inicio de historia con rutina, amenaza y riesgo.

answer.text: We used to bake bread together every morning before sunrise, and my father would sing while he worked. Then one day a letter arrived from the bank, and dread filled the shop. If we failed to pay by Friday, we would lose everything we had built.
accepted: We used to bake bread together every morning before sunrise, and my father would sing while he worked. Then one day a letter arrived from the bank, and dread filled the shop. If we failed to pay by Friday, we would lose everything we had built.

In those days my father and I would get up at four to make the bread, and the whole street used to smell of it. One morning a letter came from the bank. If we did not pay by Friday, we would lose the shop, and that thought never left me.

feedback.es: El inicio reúne rutina con used to o would, una ruptura en pasado simple y un riesgo con condicional.

origin.text: Datos: tu familia tenía una panadería y cada madrugada tu padre y tú amasaban juntos; un día llegó una carta del banco; si no pagaban antes del viernes, perderían el local. Usa used to o would, pasado simple y un condicional.

prompt.es: Lee el borrador y elige la mejora que más tensión añadiría.

choices.text: A sentence naming what they could lose if they signed
A longer description of the porch and of the road
A paragraph about the man's job and where he lived

feedback.es: El borrador tiene rutina y ruptura pero no dice qué se arriesga: nombrar lo que perderían añade más tensión que más descripción.

origin.text: Every evening we would sit on the porch and watch the road, and that was our routine for twenty years. One day a man came with some papers. We were upset.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué convierte el anuncio en una amenaza real para los niños.

choices.text: It tells them that the town hall has changed its plans.
It names a concrete loss that touches their daily lives.
It explains that the new school is too far away.

feedback.es: La amenaza se vuelve real porque se dice exactamente qué se perdería: amigos, maestros y el único lugar seguro.

origin.audio: We used to play in the school yard every afternoon. Then the town hall announced that the school would close at the end of the year. If it closed, we would lose our friends, our teachers and the only place where we felt safe.

prompt.es: Completa: «La llamada no solo alteró nuestra rutina: llenó a la familia de temor.»

feedback.es: Disrupt es alterar algo que funcionaba con normalidad, como una rutina familiar.

origin.text: Nobody expected the news. The phone call did not simply ___ our routine; it filled the whole family with dread for the rest of the week.

es: Localizar en un relato oído el fondo habitual, el giro, la reacción, la consecuencia y la reflexión, e inferir el sentido de la reflexión final.

vocabulary.es: en las secuelas, tras lo ocurrido
aceptar, hacerse a la idea de

teaching.en: The background shows the habit before anything changes: 'We used to have lunch at my grandmother's every Sunday, and we expected the afternoon to unfold just as it always had.'
teaching.es: El fondo muestra el hábito antes de que cambie algo: «Solíamos comer en casa de mi abuela todos los domingos y esperábamos que la tarde se desarrollara como siempre».
teaching.explanationEs: Background = lo que ocurría antes: suele usar used to, would o pasado continuo; unfold = desarrollarse.
segments: The background shows the habit before anything changes: 'We used to have lunch at my
grandmother's every Sunday, and we expected the afternoon to unfold just as it always had.'
teaching.audioText: The background shows the habit before anything changes: 'We used to have lunch at my grandmother's every Sunday, and we expected the afternoon to unfold just as it always had.'

teaching.en: A twist is a change nobody expects, so the narrator is often caught off guard, and words like 'until' or 'suddenly' usually announce it.
teaching.es: Un giro es un cambio que nadie espera, así que el narrador suele quedar pillado por sorpresa, y palabras como «until» o «suddenly» suelen anunciarlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Caught off guard = sorprendido sin tiempo de reaccionar; until y suddenly funcionan como señales.
segments: A twist is a change nobody expects, so the narrator is often
caught off guard, and words like 'until' or 'suddenly' usually announce it.
teaching.audioText: A twist is a change nobody expects, so the narrator is often caught off guard, and words like 'until' or 'suddenly' usually announce it.

teaching.en: The shift usually comes with a signal such as 'until one evening' or 'but then', and the verb tense moves from habit to a single event.
teaching.es: El cambio suele llegar con una señal como «hasta que una noche» o «pero entonces», y el tiempo verbal pasa del hábito a un suceso único.
teaching.explanationEs: Shift es el paso de la rutina al suceso; escucha la señal y el cambio de tiempo verbal.
segments: The shift usually comes with a signal such as 'until one evening' or
'but then', and the verb tense moves from habit to a single event.
teaching.audioText: The shift usually comes with a signal such as 'until one evening' or 'but then', and the verb tense moves from habit to a single event.

teaching.en: The reaction tells us how the character felt: 'I froze, and it took a long time for the news to sink in.'
teaching.es: La reacción nos dice cómo se sintió el personaje: «Me quedé helado y tardé mucho en asimilar la noticia».
teaching.explanationEs: Reaction = lo que siente o hace justo después del giro; sink in = calar, asimilarse.
segments: The reaction tells us how the character felt: 'I froze, and
it took a long time for the news to sink in.'
teaching.audioText: The reaction tells us how the character felt: 'I froze, and it took a long time for the news to sink in.'

teaching.en: The consequence is what changed afterwards, and in the aftermath the characters often have to come to terms with a new reality: 'Since that night, we have eaten at different times.'
teaching.es: La consecuencia es lo que cambió después, y tras lo ocurrido los personajes suelen tener que aceptar una nueva realidad: «Desde aquella noche, hemos cenado a horas distintas».
teaching.explanationEs: Consequence suele ir con since y el presente perfecto; in the aftermath = después de un suceso importante.
segments: The consequence is what changed afterwards, and in the aftermath the characters often have to come
to terms with a new reality: 'Since that night, we have eaten at different times.'
teaching.audioText: The consequence is what changed afterwards, and in the aftermath the characters often have to come to terms with a new reality: 'Since that night, we have eaten at different times.'

teaching.en: The reflection closes the story with meaning: 'Looking back, I realise that, slowly, everything began to fall into place.'
teaching.es: La reflexión cierra la historia con sentido: «Mirando atrás, me doy cuenta de que, poco a poco, todo empezó a encajar».
teaching.explanationEs: Reflection es la idea final; «looking back» es su señal más frecuente; fall into place = encajar.
segments: The reflection closes the story with meaning: 'Looking back, I
realise that, slowly, everything began to fall into place.'
teaching.audioText: The reflection closes the story with meaning: 'Looking back, I realise that, slowly, everything began to fall into place.'

prompt.es: Elige la señal que anuncia el giro de la historia.

choices.text: every night
nobody ever checked
until one evening

feedback.es: «Until one evening» rompe la rutina y anuncia el cambio; las otras dos expresiones pertenecen al fondo habitual.

hint.es: Busca la expresión que rompe la rutina.

origin.text: We used to eat dinner together every night, and nobody ever checked a phone, until one evening a call from the hospital changed the mood of the whole house.

The narrator stayed angry and refused to forgive him.

origin.audio: We used to spend every Saturday at my uncle's farm, and I never imagined that anything there could change. Until the day he sold it without telling anyone. I was caught off guard, and I stayed angry for months. In the aftermath, we drifted apart, but last spring I went to see him in the little flat he had moved to. Looking back, I understand that the farm was simply too big for a man of seventy.

The reaction to the twist

origin.text: My hands went cold, and for a long moment I could not hear anything around me. I just sat there, staring at the table, while everybody else carried on talking about lunch.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sentido da la narradora a su reflexión final.

choices.text: She fears her colleagues more than she fears speaking at all.
She believes that large audiences are almost always unfriendly.
She was afraid of making mistakes in front of people.

feedback.es: La reflexión separa el miedo al público del miedo a equivocarse delante de la gente: lo que temía era el error visible, no a las personas.

origin.audio: I used to be terrified of speaking in public. Then, out of the blue, my boss asked me to present our results to two hundred people. My legs were trembling, but I spoke. Afterwards, several colleagues came to thank me, and the following month I was offered a new role. Looking back, I see that the fear was never really about the audience. It was about making mistakes in front of people.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige por qué menciona que varios colegas fueron a darle las gracias.

choices.text: To show the positive consequences of the twist.
To explain why her legs were trembling so badly.
To introduce the background of the whole story.

feedback.es: Los agradecimientos y el nuevo puesto son lo que cambió después del giro: forman la consecuencia de la anécdota.

origin.audio: I used to be terrified of speaking in public. Then, out of the blue, my boss asked me to present our results to two hundred people. My legs were trembling, but I spoke. prompt.es: Completa: «De repente, el casero llamó y canceló el contrato.»

feedback.es: Out of the blue es la expresión para algo totalmente inesperado, como el giro que rompe los planes.

origin.text: We had planned every detail of the move for months. Then, out of the ___, the landlord called and cancelled the contract.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Después, tuvo que aceptar lo ocurrido.»

answer.text: In the aftermath she had to come to terms with it

prompt.es: Lee la reflexión y elige qué actitud muestra la narradora hacia el revés.

choices.text: She still blames the client for ending the contract with them.
She now sees it as painful but in the end useful.
She regrets not having looked for customers abroad earlier.

feedback.es: Dice que fue lo peor, pero reconoce que la obligó a buscar clientes fuera y así sobrevivieron: ve el revés como doloroso y a la larga útil.

origin.text: I used to think that losing the contract was the worst thing that could happen to a small company like ours. We were caught off guard, and for weeks the office felt very sad. But, looking back, it forced us to look for customers abroad, and that is how we saved the business.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué revela la conducta del narrador.

choices.text: Anger directed at the person who had given him the bad news.
Relief that the long wait was finally over.
Shock so deep that he could not speak or think clearly.

feedback.es: Soltar la taza, huir sin hablar y conducir en silencio muestran una reacción de shock profundo, no de enfado ni de alivio.

origin.audio: I dropped my cup, ran to the car without a word and drove for an hour with the radio off, not able to believe what I had heard.

prompt.es: Completa: «Años después, mirando atrás, todo empezó a encajar.»

feedback.es: Fall into place describe cómo las piezas de una historia encajan con el tiempo, típico de la reflexión final.

origin.text: Nothing made sense at the time. But years later, looking back, everything began to ___ into place, and I understood why she had made that decision.

es: Narrar una anécdota de 160 a 210 palabras que combine hábito de fondo, giro y reacción con marcadores de secuencia, suspense y una reflexión final.

vocabulary.es: lo siguiente que supe, y de pronto
hacer una pausa para dar efecto

teaching.en: Open with a time marker such as 'In those days' and describe the habit: 'In those days, we would walk to school together and race the ferry.'
teaching.es: Empieza con un marcador temporal como «En aquellos días» y describe el hábito: «En aquellos días, íbamos juntos al colegio y competíamos con el ferry».
teaching.explanationEs: Un marker ordena el tiempo del relato; in those days sitúa un hábito pasado.
segments: Open with a time marker such as 'In those days' and describe the habit:
'In those days, we would walk to school together and race the ferry.'
teaching.audioText: Open with a time marker such as 'In those days' and describe the habit: 'In those days, we would walk to school together and race the ferry.'

teaching.en: Gradually, small things began to change, and the next thing I knew, nobody in the house was speaking at dinner.
teaching.es: Poco a poco, pequeñas cosas empezaron a cambiar y, de pronto, nadie en la casa hablaba durante la cena.
teaching.explanationEs: Gradually marca un cambio lento; the next thing I knew resume un salto brusco.
segments: Gradually, small things began to change, and the next thing
I knew, nobody in the house was speaking at dinner.
teaching.audioText: Gradually, small things began to change, and the next thing I knew, nobody in the house was speaking at dinner.

teaching.en: Meanwhile, my brother was mending the boat, unaware of what was coming, and the contrast between his calm and my unease helps to build up suspense.
teaching.es: Mientras tanto, mi hermano arreglaba el barco, sin saber lo que venía, y el contraste entre su calma y mi inquietud ayuda a acumular suspense.
teaching.explanationEs: Meanwhile une dos acciones simultáneas; va con coma; build up = ir acumulando tensión.
segments: Meanwhile, my brother was mending the boat, unaware of what was coming, and
the contrast between his calm and my unease helps to build up suspense.
teaching.audioText: Meanwhile, my brother was mending the boat, unaware of what was coming, and the contrast between his calm and my unease helps to build up suspense.

teaching.en: To keep the audience in suspense, delay the important detail: 'I opened the door, and then, all of a sudden, I saw...'
teaching.es: Para mantener al público en vilo, retrasa el detalle importante: «Abrí la puerta y entonces, de repente, vi…».
teaching.explanationEs: Los puntos suspensivos y las pausas crean espera; all of a sudden anuncia el giro.
segments: To keep the audience in suspense, delay the important detail: 'I
opened the door, and then, all of a sudden, I saw...'
teaching.audioText: To keep the audience in suspense, delay the important detail: 'I opened the door, and then, all of a sudden, I saw...'

teaching.en: Reveal the twist in one short sentence, preferably after a pause for effect: 'The door was already open.'
teaching.es: Revela el giro en una sola frase corta, preferiblemente tras una pausa para dar efecto: «La puerta ya estaba abierta».
teaching.explanationEs: Reveal = mostrar lo oculto; la frase corta golpea más; pause for effect = silencio buscado.
segments: Reveal the twist in one short sentence, preferably after
a pause for effect: 'The door was already open.'
teaching.audioText: Reveal the twist in one short sentence, preferably after a pause for effect: 'The door was already open.'

teaching.en: Eventually, she told me everything, and little did I know that her story would change the way I saw the whole family.
teaching.es: Al final me lo contó todo, y yo no sabía que su historia cambiaría la forma en que veía a toda la familia.
teaching.explanationEs: Eventually = con el tiempo, al final; no significa «eventualmente». Little did I know anticipa el giro.
segments: Eventually, she told me everything, and little did I know that
her story would change the way I saw the whole family.
teaching.audioText: Eventually, she told me everything, and little did I know that her story would change the way I saw the whole family.

prompt.es: Escucha la anécdota y elige cómo se revela el final.

origin.audio: In those days I used to deliver newspapers before school. Gradually the streets became quieter, and every morning I felt as if someone was following me. Meanwhile, my bike light was failing. One dark morning, the next thing I knew, I heard footsteps right behind me. I turned around very slowly. It was only a dog, carrying my missing newspaper in its teeth.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mientras tanto, mi hermana llamaba un taxi sin saberlo.»

feedback.es: Meanwhile une dos acciones que ocurren a la vez y va al principio de la frase con coma.

origin.text: I was packing my bags in the bedroom. ___, my sister was calling a taxi downstairs, unaware that I had changed my mind.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que revela el giro de forma breve y eficaz.

choices.text: After a long time of thinking, I finally understood that the key had been in my own pocket, which surprised me greatly.
Maybe the key was in my pocket, or possibly in a drawer I had not checked yet.

feedback.es: La revelación funciona mejor en una frase corta y directa; las otras la diluyen con explicaciones o dudas.

origin.text: I spent the whole night searching the house for the missing key. I checked every drawer, every coat and every shoe. At dawn, exhausted, I sat down on the stairs, and only then did I notice where it had been all along.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué efecto crea la narradora con el final del relato.

choices.text: A lasting mystery that the narrator decides not to solve.
A happy ending that solves the mystery of the letter.
A warning about the danger of opening other people's post.

feedback.es: Acaba con una carta para un desconocido y una abuela que sigue mirando a la puerta, sin explicar nada: deja el misterio abierto.

origin.audio: Every evening my grandmother would sit at the window, reading old letters. Gradually she stopped, and the letters gathered dust on the table. One day I found a letter in her basket, still closed. It was addressed to a man I had never heard of, and the date on the envelope was forty years old. I never asked her about it, although I wanted to so badly that I could hardly sleep. But since then, whenever the post arrives, I catch her looking at the door.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué sugiere la última frase de la narradora.

choices.text: That she has completely forgotten who that man was.
That she still hopes for something linked to that letter.
That the post always arrives late in the village.

feedback.es: Que mire a la puerta cada vez que llega el correo sugiere que aún espera algo, aunque la narradora nunca lo diga: es una inferencia.

feedback.es: Gradually marca un cambio lento y progresivo, ideal para acumular tensión antes del giro.

prompt.es: Escribe una anécdota de 160 a 210 palabras con hábito, giro y consecuencia.

answer.text: In those days, my grandmother and I would bake bread every Sunday morning. She never used a recipe, and the whole house smelled of warm bread until noon. Gradually, I noticed that she was forgetting the steps, but she laughed it off, and I did not want to ask any questions. Meanwhile, I was busy with school and my friends. One Sunday, she did not come out of her room. I waited in the kitchen, and my hands were cold. Then I saw her sitting on the bed, pale and confused. 'I do not remember the recipe,' she whispered. Eventually, I sat beside her, and we wrote the steps down together. Since that day, I have read the recipe aloud every Sunday. Looking back, I think that quiet morning taught me that love can also mean remembering for someone else.
accepted: In those days, my grandmother and I would bake bread every Sunday morning. She never used a recipe, and the whole house smelled of warm bread until noon. Gradually, I noticed that she was forgetting the steps, but she laughed it off, and I did not want to ask any questions. Meanwhile, I was busy with school and my friends. One Sunday, she did not come out of her room. I waited in the kitchen, and my hands were cold. Then I saw her sitting on the bed, pale and confused. 'I do not remember the recipe,' she whispered. Eventually, I sat beside her, and we wrote the steps down together. Since that day, I have read the recipe aloud every Sunday. Looking back, I think that quiet morning taught me that love can also mean remembering for someone else.

In those days, every Sunday my grandmother and I would make bread together, and she always said that she did not need a book. Little by little, I noticed that she was forgetting the order of the steps. At the same time, I was too busy with my friends to ask her about it. Then, one Sunday, the kitchen was silent. I found her sitting at the table, pale and confused, looking at the flour as if she had never seen it. Finally, I took her hand, and we wrote the recipe on a piece of paper. Since then, I have read it aloud to her every Sunday. Looking back, I realise that I was the one who learned the most that day.

feedback.es: La anécdota combina fondo habitual, marcadores de secuencia, un giro con suspense, la consecuencia y una reflexión final.

origin.text: Datos: cada domingo tu abuela y tú hacían pan; poco a poco notaste que olvidaba los pasos; un domingo no salió de su cuarto; la encontraste sentada y confundida, y te dijo que no recordaba la receta; desde ese día le lees la receta en voz alta cada domingo. Usa marcadores, suspense y una reflexión final.

prompt.es: Lee las dos versiones y elige qué técnica usa la segunda para crear suspense.

choices.text: It describes the key in far more detail than the first version does.
It tells the reader in advance what the box contains.
It builds up the moment and delays the object until the end.

feedback.es: La segunda versión retrasa la aparición del objeto con pausas y detalles, y lo revela al final de la frase: así crea suspense.

origin.text: Version A: 'I opened the box. Inside was a key.' Version B: 'I opened the box slowly. For a moment there was nothing but silence, and then, right at the back, something small and cold caught the light: a key.'

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere la última frase sobre la narradora.

choices.text: That she later saw the decision from her mother's point of view.
That she still blames her mother for selling the old family house.
That she has no memory of the summers by the sea.

feedback.es: «It was years before I understood what it had cost her» indica que con el tiempo entendió a su madre: es la reflexión que cierra el relato.

origin.audio: We used to spend every summer by the sea. Then, all of a sudden, my mother announced that we were selling the house. Eventually we said goodbye to the beach, but I stayed angry for years. It was years before I understood what that decision had cost her.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Yo no sabía que mi vida estaba a punto de cambiar.»

answer.text: Little did I know that my life was about to change

feedback.es: Little did I know va al inicio y anticipa el giro; tras él, el orden normal de la frase.

title.es: Una historia que vale la pena repetir

es: Construir y contar una historia con gancho, conflicto, resolución e idea final, cuidando un detalle vívido, y responder a dos preguntas de un oyente.

vocabulary.es: situar la escena, preparar el escenario
pintar un cuadro, hacer ver algo
subir la tensión, aumentar lo que está en juego

teaching.en: A story people want to retell begins with a hook, for example 'I got on the wrong train, and it changed everything,' and then you set the scene in a few well-chosen words.
teaching.es: Una historia que la gente quiere volver a contar empieza con un gancho, por ejemplo «Me subí al tren equivocado y lo cambió todo», y después sitúas la escena con unas pocas palabras bien elegidas.
teaching.explanationEs: Retell = contar de nuevo; el gancho despierta curiosidad en la primera frase; set the scene = preparar el escenario.
segments: A story people want to retell begins with a hook, for example 'I got on the wrong
train, and it changed everything,' and then you set the scene in a few well-chosen words.
teaching.audioText: A story people want to retell begins with a hook, for example 'I got on the wrong train, and it changed everything,' and then you set the scene in a few well-chosen words.

teaching.en: The conflict is the problem the character cannot ignore, and the best storytellers raise the stakes by showing exactly what will be lost if it stays unsolved.
teaching.es: El conflicto es el problema que el personaje no puede ignorar, y los mejores narradores suben la tensión mostrando exactamente qué se perderá si sigue sin resolverse.
teaching.explanationEs: Conflict = el problema central; raise the stakes = aumentar lo que está en juego.
segments: The conflict is the problem the character cannot ignore, and the best storytellers raise
the stakes by showing exactly what will be lost if it stays unsolved.
teaching.audioText: The conflict is the problem the character cannot ignore, and the best storytellers raise the stakes by showing exactly what will be lost if it stays unsolved.

teaching.en: One vivid detail, such as the smell of oranges on the platform, can paint a picture more effectively than a whole paragraph of general description.
teaching.es: Un detalle vívido, como el olor a naranjas en el andén, puede pintar un cuadro con más eficacia que todo un párrafo de descripción general.
teaching.explanationEs: Vivid es gráfico y sensorial; paint a picture = hacer que el oyente vea la escena.
segments: One vivid detail, such as the smell of oranges on the platform, can
paint a picture more effectively than a whole paragraph of general description.
teaching.audioText: One vivid detail, such as the smell of oranges on the platform, can paint a picture more effectively than a whole paragraph of general description.

teaching.en: The resolution shows how the problem ended, and it should feel earned, as in 'A stranger shared her map, and in the end I found my way.'
teaching.es: La resolución muestra cómo terminó el problema y debe sentirse merecida, como en «Una desconocida compartió su mapa y al final encontré mi camino».
teaching.explanationEs: Resolution = el desenlace del conflicto; debe salir de lo contado, no de la nada.
segments: The resolution shows how the problem ended, and it should feel earned, as in
'A stranger shared her map, and in the end I found my way.'
teaching.audioText: The resolution shows how the problem ended, and it should feel earned, as in 'A stranger shared her map, and in the end I found my way.'

teaching.en: End with a takeaway that the listener can repeat, such as 'Sometimes the wrong train takes you to the right place,' a line that rounds off the story and sticks in the mind.
teaching.es: Termina con una idea final que el oyente pueda repetir, como «A veces el tren equivocado te lleva al lugar correcto», una frase que remata la historia y se queda grabada en la memoria.
teaching.explanationEs: Takeaway es lo que el oyente se lleva y repetirá; round off = rematar; stick in the mind = quedarse grabado.
segments: End with a takeaway that the listener can repeat, such as 'Sometimes the wrong train takes you
to the right place,' a line that rounds off the story and sticks in the mind.
teaching.audioText: End with a takeaway that the listener can repeat, such as 'Sometimes the wrong train takes you to the right place,' a line that rounds off the story and sticks in the mind.

teaching.en: If the last line echoes the hook, the story comes full circle, and the audience feels that everything has been neatly brought together.
teaching.es: Si la última frase se hace eco del gancho, la historia cierra el círculo y el público siente que todo ha quedado bien atado.
teaching.explanationEs: Come full circle = volver al punto de partida con un sentido nuevo.
segments: If the last line echoes the hook, the story comes full circle,
and the audience feels that everything has been neatly brought together.
teaching.audioText: If the last line echoes the hook, the story comes full circle, and the audience feels that everything has been neatly brought together.

Forty years ago, a stranger's suitcase changed my father's life.
I want to tell you something about my father and a suitcase.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo se resuelve el conflicto de la historia.

choices.text: A street musician found him and brought him back to her.
A police officer heard her and took her to the stalls.

feedback.es: El conflicto (el hermano perdido) se resuelve cuando ella lo oye reír y lo encuentra junto a un músico callejero; nadie lo trae de vuelta.

origin.audio: When I was twelve, I lost my little brother at a street festival. For ten terrible minutes, I searched every stall, asking everyone if they had seen a boy in a green jacket. The music seemed to get louder, and my legs felt heavy. Then I heard him laughing. He was sitting on a box beside a street musician, wearing a paper hat twice his size. From that day on, I never let go of his hand in a crowd, and even now, at thirty, I sometimes reach for it.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una función: abre con curiosidad, plantea el problema, lo resuelve y deja una idea para llevarse.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué la tía cuenta esta historia en las bodas.

To show that an accident can lead to lasting love.

origin.audio: My aunt tells the same story at every wedding. When she was twenty, she got on the wrong bus in Quito and ended up three hours away, in a village with no hotel. It was raining, and her only money was a ten-dollar note. A woman let her sleep above the bakery in exchange for help with the morning bread. She stayed a week, then a year, and then for the rest of her life: the woman's son is now my uncle. She always ends with the same line: nobody plans the best things in life.

prompt.es: Cuenta una historia familiar con gancho, conflicto, resolución e idea final.

answer.text: Thirty years ago, my father arrived in Madrid with one suitcase and a single phone number. At the airport, someone took his bag by mistake, and he left with a stranger's suitcase. Inside there were no clothes at all, only an old guitar. He had no money, so he played in the street to pay for his first room. One evening, the owner of a small restaurant stopped to listen and offered him a job. Was he scared? Terribly, but the music kept his hands busy. Did he ever find his suitcase? Never, and he says that he does not miss it. The takeaway? Sometimes the wrong suitcase is the right luck. Today he still plays in that restaurant, and the story has come full circle, because it began with a stranger and a bag.

Forty years ago my father left home with one small suitcase and the address of a cousin in Madrid. At the airport, another passenger picked up his bag by mistake, so my father went home with a stranger's suitcase. When he opened it, there were no clothes inside, only an old guitar. He had no money, so he played in the street to pay his rent. One night, the owner of a restaurant heard him and gave him a job. Were you scared, Dad? Of course I was afraid, he told me, but playing calmed me down. Did you ever find your suitcase? Never, and I never missed it. Here is the lesson: sometimes a mistake turns out to be your luck. Today he still plays in that restaurant, exactly where the story began.

feedback.es: La historia tiene gancho, conflicto (la maleta cambiada), resolución (el trabajo en el restaurante), respuestas a las dos preguntas del oyente e idea final.

origin.text: Datos: tu padre llegó a Madrid hace treinta años con una maleta y un solo número de teléfono; en el aeropuerto alguien se llevó su maleta por error y él salió con otra que solo tenía una guitarra vieja; tocó en la calle para pagar su primera habitación; el dueño de un restaurante le ofreció trabajo. Un oyente pregunta: «Was he scared?» y «Did he ever find his suitcase?». Responde a ambas dentro del texto y cierra con una idea final.

origin.text: Most people believe that a story needs a surprising plot. In my experience, what makes listeners retell a story is something much smaller: a detail they can see and a line they can repeat. The plot can be forgotten; the picture and the sentence stay.
